method: Direct view_image inspection of the saved native output against the unchanged prospective testcase. Arm's initial observations had been received, but its final verdict had not been read.

gates.evidence: Identification portrait, notebook, pen and two-person exchange clearly support inquiry rather than ticket purchase. The investigator looks toward the speaker's face, not the indicated map point required in this gate's attention field. No visible pen-hover gap establishes the separately planned paused-note relation.

The witness forearm, finger and contact on the map are visible. The fingertip is on the upper-right route branch, while the dock-shaped marked structure lies left of the fork. The specifically requested dock/landing target is not established by a generic map touch.

A clear portrait print supplies a person as case target, and its edge is held. The photograph is held by the arm on the viewer's left (the front-facing investigator's right), while the pen belongs to the other arm; the declared left-hand photograph ownership is reversed. The depicted person is not identified as a real individual.

A staffed ticket booth, timetable, counter materials and an empty landing/gangway behind the exchange provide a coherent ferry-work setting. This supports the witness opportunity context, not the actual last-crossing chronology.
The investigator's face is clearly visible and the dark bob and wispy fringe correspond to the supplied portrait's visible appearance. No identity, age or biography is inferred.
The inquiry story reads clearly, but the required gaze-to-map, dock-target contact and exact photo-hand ownership do not all pass. The full C1–C4 conjunction therefore fails.
